user.text:
The `agenda` package in /app expands recurring calendar events into dated instances, and it has bugs. Some of its unit tests fail. From /app, run them with:

    python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

Fix the package code under /app/agenda so that it follows the rules in /app/docs (start with /app/docs/overview.md). Passing the unit tests is not enough: the package will also be run on other events, zones and reporting windows, and every document it writes must follow the docs. Do not change anything under /app/tests, /app/data or /app/docs.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

| `BYMONTHDAY` | comma list of 1 to 31 and -1 to -31 | none |
| `BYMONTH` | comma list of 1 to 12 | none |

"""Local start times generated by a rule (rules.md sections 4 and 5)."""

from collections.abc import Iterator
from datetime import date, datetime

from ..zones import Zone
from .parse import Rule
from .periods import period_dates, period_start

# A rule whose periods never hold a date (BYMONTHDAY=30;BYMONTH=2) would
# otherwise be searched up to the horizon one empty period at a time.
MAX_PERIODS = 50000


def past_until(rule: Rule, local: datetime, zone: Zone) -> bool:
    if rule.until is None:
        return False
    kind, value = rule.until
    if kind == "date":
        return local.date() > value
    return zone.to_utc(local) > value


def occurrences(rule: Rule, dtstart: datetime, zone: Zone, horizon: date) -> Iterator[datetime]:
    """DTSTART, then every later start the rule generates, in order, until
    UNTIL or the first period that begins after the horizon. COUNT is left to
    the caller."""
    yield dtstart
    for k in range(MAX_PERIODS):
        if period_start(rule, dtstart.date(), k) > horizon:
            return
        for d in period_dates(rule, dtstart.date(), k):
            local = datetime.combine(d, dtstart.time())
            if local <= dtstart:
                continue
            if past_until(rule, local, zone):
                return
            yield local
